topic: T4_fpp_companion - False-positive probability and companion constraints
summary: FINAL: default TRICERATOPS FPP of the 3.18 d signal is 0.03-0.04 (means 0.030-0.044 over 15 S32+S98 configurations, 4-20 runs of 1e6 draws each; per-run 0.026-0.048); '0.031 +- 0.003 (0.031-0.034, three folds)' is superseded (one of those 'folds' is an input variant, C082). 10-min bins raise FPP_A by 20-26% (not symmetric). NFPP < 1e-6 everywhere (<= 7e-10 for S32+S98). STP is >= 99.7% of FPP; 84-96% (about 90%) comes from companions > 0.38 Msun; removing them at all separations gives 0.002-0.007. MOLUSC-mode values (~0.005) scale as 1/N and must not be quoted; the properly normalised Gaia-RUWE-constrained value is 0.0030 +- 0.0008 (20 runs). B: 0.13-0.21 (not in the revision). No validation: G21 requires FPP < 0.015 and NFPP < 1e-3, calibrated for circular orbits. Companion limits: O = +0.003 mag excludes Gaia-blended (<~0.2 arcsec) companions > ~0.38 Msun at 2 sigma (0.35-0.42 depending on scatter); C* normal (SOAR 0/38); RUWE 1.214 at the 61st percentile; Gaia RVs give 95% K < 1.16 km/s, excluding an eclipsing stellar companion of the target (the low p-value is not RV variability). Circular orbit needs a host >= ~0.52 Msun, leaving 0.15-0.38 Msun hosts with e >~ 0.2-0.6 as the main open scenario. Manuscript: one MINOR scope fix ('of the target') and one optional clarification. Open (non-blocking): the companion scenario and chance-aligned sources need speckle/AO imaging.

facts.supersedes: the MOLUSC-mode values (audit 0.0047 +- 0.0027 at 5 Gyr, 0.0054 +- 0.0032 at 1 Gyr, 20 runs each; U 0.0055 +- 0.0036, 10 runs; pubprep '0.005 +- 0.003') are superseded as the constrained number because they scale as 1/N (see FPP.A_molusc_mode). The blended-only cut (<0.2 arcsec) alone gives 0.024 +- 0.004 (R5, 5 runs) and must not be called 'constrained FPP ~0.002'.
facts.manuscript_form: About 90\% of the FPP comes from companions above $0.38\,M_\odot$: excluding them (a post hoc prior cut) gives FPP $\approx0.002$--0.007.
facts.notes: The cut at all separations is supported by overluminosity (<~0.2 arcsec, 2 sigma), the BP/RP excess C* (0.2-2 arcsec, empirical 95% UL 7.6% miss rate) and resolved Gaia sources (>~1.2 arcsec). Keeping the 7.6% miss rate at 0.2-2 arcsec would raise it by at most ~0.003 (0.076 x 0.034); for the MOLUSC-mode analogue R4 found 0.0010 -> 0.0018-0.0020.

Target RUWE 1.214 is above Way's Regression Sample cut (ruwe < 1.2), so O is an out-of-sample prediction (R4). The limit of 0.38 is the conservative end of the 0.35-0.38 range implied by the quoted 0.05-0.07 scatter.

facts.quantity: remaining (not excluded) false-positive scenario for the 3.18 d signal
facts.value: main: a planet on an eccentric orbit (e >~ 0.2-0.6) around an unresolved bound companion of 0.15-0.38 Msun at ~0.1-2.2 arcsec (3.6-78 au, TRICERATOPS' default window); secondary, statistically small: an eclipsing binary or transiting body on a chance-aligned background star unresolved by Gaia (<~2 arcsec at dG ~4-8)
facts.uncertainty: TRICERATOPS assigns the main channel FPP ~0.002-0.007 after the 0.38 Msun cut; BTP + BEB <= 1.2e-4 in any A variant (~2e-5 in S32+S98 folds)
facts.supersedes: M FALSE_POSITIVE_MATRIX row 18 'planet on unresolved companion OPEN' (now restricted in mass and e) and row 20 'chance-aligned unresolved source OPEN' (statistically small, observationally open).
facts.manuscript_form: leave a planet on an eccentric orbit around a 0.15--0.38\,$M_\odot$ bound companion as the main false-positive scenario not yet excluded
facts.notes: TRICERATOPS already covers: STP (eccentric orbits included), SEB/SEBx2P (bound EB), DTP (planet on target diluted by a chance-aligned star, counted as planet), BTP/BEB/BEBx2P (background host), NTP/NEB (resolved neighbours). What it does not apply by default: the overluminosity/C* cut. Closure needs speckle/AO imaging (covers 0.02-2 arcsec) and RV monitoring for a <~1-3 au.
